method_card.title: Grid References (4 and 6 Figure)
steps: Easting first: read along the bottom of the map
Northing second: read up the side of the map
Four figures name the whole square
Six figures add a tenth to each half
method_card.content:
Grid references locate places using the numbered lines printed on a map. Read the easting (along the bottom) first, then the northing (up the side): along the corridor, up the stairs.

A four figure reference names a whole square, 1 km by 1 km. Take the easting of the line down the left of the square, then the northing of the line along its bottom.

A six figure reference pins a point to the nearest 100 m. After each two figure line number, add how many tenths across (or up) the square the feature sits.

Watch out for: writing the northing first, and using the lines on the right and top of the square instead of the left and bottom.
method_card.example:
Question: A church sits halfway across square 3832 and three tenths up. Give the six figure reference.

Easting: line 38, plus 5 tenths, gives 385. Northing: line 32, plus 3 tenths, gives 323. Reference: 385323.

exam_context.frequency: Almost every year, an essential skill

gold.hint: Trace Towneley Holmes Road until it reaches Todmorden Road, then read the easting and its tenth before the northing and its tenth.
gold.display: Give the six-figure grid reference of the point where Towneley Holmes Road meets Todmorden Road.

misconceptions.message: You have led with the northing half. The three figures read along the bottom of the map always come first.
misconceptions.note: northing half placed first

misconceptions.message: You have named the whole square instead of a point inside it. Each half still needs its tenth adding on.
misconceptions.note: four figure answer given where six were asked

guided_steps.say: Find the junction where Towneley Holmes Road meets Todmorden Road on the map. Six figures means two readings each way: the grid line, then the tenths.

guided_steps.pre: Start with the square it sits in. Read the two figure number of the grid line down its left side, from the numbers along the bottom of the map, and type it.
guided_steps.hint: The easting line is the one touching the left edge of the square, numbered along the bottom of the map.
guided_steps.done: That is the first two figures of the easting.

guided_steps.pre: Picture that square split into ten strips from left to right. Type how many tenths across the square the feature sits, to the nearest whole tenth.
guided_steps.hint: Halfway across the square is 5 tenths, so judge the position against the middle.

guided_steps.pre: Now the northing. Read the two figure number of the grid line along the bottom of the square, from the numbers up the side, and type it.
guided_steps.hint: The northing line is the one touching the bottom of the square, numbered up the side of the map.
guided_steps.done: That is the first two figures of the northing.

guided_steps.pre: Now split the square into ten strips from bottom to top. Type how many tenths up the square the feature sits.
guided_steps.hint: Halfway up the square is 5 tenths, so judge the position against the middle.

guided_steps.pre: Put the three easting figures first, then the three northing figures, and type the six figure reference.
guided_steps.hint: Line number then tenth for the easting, then line number then tenth for the northing, with no gap.

guided_steps.pre: Check it: type the last three figures of the reference you just wrote.
guided_steps.hint: Copy them straight off your own answer.
guided_steps.done: Those three must be the northing: the line read up the side, then its tenth. If they are not, the two halves have swapped and the point moves right off the map.

misconceptions.message: You have led with the pair read up the side of the map. A grid reference always starts with the figures read along the bottom.
misconceptions.note: northing pair placed first

misconceptions.message: You have read the lines on the right hand side and the top of the square. Both figures come from the lines that touch the square on its left and along its bottom.
misconceptions.note: square identified by its top right corner

bronze.hint: Find the two station symbols, then read the grid line down the left of their square before the line along its bottom.

guided_steps.say: Find the two train station symbols on the map. Nothing here is a calculation, it is all reading numbers off the edges.

guided_steps.pre: Look at the square they share. A vertical grid line runs down its left side. Read that line's two figure number from the numbers along the bottom of the map and type it.
guided_steps.hint: The easting is the line touching the left edge of the square, and its number is printed along the bottom of the map.
guided_steps.done: That is the easting, and it always comes first.

guided_steps.pre: Now the horizontal grid line along the bottom of that same square. Read its two figure number from the numbers up the side of the map and type it.
guided_steps.hint: The northing is the line touching the bottom of the square, and its number is printed up the side.
guided_steps.done: That is the northing, and it always comes second.

guided_steps.pre: Join the two pairs, easting first, into one four figure reference and type it.
guided_steps.hint: Along the corridor before up the stairs: the pair read along the bottom of the map goes first.

guided_steps.pre: Check it: type the last two figures of the reference you just wrote.
guided_steps.hint: Copy them straight off your own answer, there is nothing new to work out.
guided_steps.done: Those two must be the line you read up the side of the map. If they are not, the halves are the wrong way round and the reference lands in a different square.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Name the whole square a labelled feature sits in: a four figure reference, easting pair then northing pair.
problem_bank.silver_description: Pin a labelled feature inside its square with six figures by adding tenths across and tenths up.
problem_bank.gold_description: Work out where an unlabelled feature is, such as a junction, a fork or a river merge, then give its six figure reference.

steps.label: Step 1: Find the feature
steps.content: Locate Burnley town centre on the map , look for where the main roads converge in the middle of the built-up area.

steps.label: Step 2: Read the easting (along the corridor)
steps.content:
Remember: "Along the corridor, up the stairs" , read the horizontal axis first.

Find the easting (bottom axis number) of the left edge of the grid square containing Burnley town centre. This is 83.

steps.label: Step 3: Read the northing (up the stairs)
steps.content: Now read the northing (side axis number) of the bottom edge of the grid square. This is 32.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content:
Combine easting + northing: 8332

A four-figure grid reference identifies a whole 1 km × 1 km grid square.

worked_examples.question: What is the four-figure grid reference of the grid square containing Burnley town centre?

steps.label: Step 1: Find the feature
steps.content: Locate the M65 motorway (the thick green road running roughly east–west). Find where it crosses the railway line (black dashes with cross-marks).

steps.label: Step 2: Read the easting to the left grid line
steps.content: The left grid line of the square is 83. Now estimate how many tenths across the square the crossing point lies. The crossing is roughly 5 tenths across, giving an easting of 835.

steps.label: Step 3: Read the northing to the bottom grid line
steps.content: The bottom grid line is 33. Estimate how many tenths up the square the crossing lies. It is roughly 4 tenths up, giving a northing of 334.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content:
Six-figure grid reference: 835334

A six-figure reference pinpoints a location to within 100 m × 100 m, much more precise than a four-figure reference.

worked_examples.question: Give the six-figure grid reference of the point where the M65 motorway crosses the railway line.

steps.label: Step 1: Break down the reference
steps.content:
Split the six-figure reference into its parts:

  • Easting: 838 → grid line 83, then 8 tenths across
  • Northing: 326 → grid line 32, then 6 tenths up

steps.label: Step 2: Locate the easting
steps.content: Find grid line 83 on the bottom axis. Move 8 tenths of the way towards grid line 84 (almost at the right edge of the square).

steps.label: Step 3: Locate the northing
steps.content: Find grid line 32 on the side axis. Move 6 tenths of the way up towards grid line 33 (just past halfway up the square).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content:
Where the easting and northing intersect, you should find Burnley Manchester Road railway station (identified by the station symbol along the railway line in the south-east part of the town centre).

Tip: When working backwards from a reference, always plot both coordinates separately before finding the intersection.

worked_examples.question: A feature is located at grid reference 838326. What feature is found at this location on the Burnley map?

bronze.title: Bronze: name the whole square
steps: Find the feature, then look at the square it sits inside.
Read the two figure number of the grid line down the left side of that square, using the numbers along the bottom of the map.
Read the two figure number of the line along the bottom of the square, using the numbers up the side.
Write the easting pair first, then the northing pair, with no gap.

example.question: A farm sits in the square whose left hand line is 27 and whose bottom line is 14. Give the four figure grid reference.

steps.label: Read the easting
steps.content: The line down the left of the square is 27

steps.label: Read the northing
steps.content: The line along the bottom of the square is 14

steps.label: Check the order
steps.content: Easting leads, so the pair read along the bottom of the map goes first

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: 2714

silver.title: Silver: pin a point inside the square
steps: Start with the four figure square, exactly as at bronze.
Split the square into ten strips across and judge how many tenths from the left line the feature sits. Add that digit to the easting.
Do the same upwards from the bottom line and add that digit to the northing.
Six figures in all: three for the easting, then three for the northing.

example.question: A post office sits 4 tenths across and 7 tenths up square 5238. Give the six figure grid reference.

steps.label: Build the easting
steps.content: Line 52, plus 4 tenths across, gives 524

steps.label: Build the northing
steps.content: Line 38, plus 7 tenths up, gives 387

steps.label: Check the halves
steps.content: Three figures each, easting half first

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: 524387

gold.title: Gold: find the feature, then reference it
steps: The feature is described rather than labelled: a junction, a bridge, a fork, a river merge. Trace both things until they meet.
Mark the meeting point itself, not the nearest label or name.
Then give the six figure reference of that point in the usual order.

example.question: A road crosses a stream 8 tenths across and 2 tenths up square 4419. Give the six figure grid reference of the crossing.

steps.label: Locate the crossing
steps.content: Take the point where the two lines actually meet

steps.label: Build both halves
steps.content: Easting 44 plus 8 tenths gives 448; northing 19 plus 2 tenths gives 192

steps.label: Check the order
steps.content: Easting half leads, northing half follows

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: 448192

opener.display: You have parked in a multi storey car park. The floor is marked out in a grid: columns are numbered along the bottom, rows are numbered up the side. You want to text a friend where the car is.

steps.say: No method needed yet. Just look at the picture and count.

steps.pre: Count along the bottom. Type the column number your car is parked in.
steps.hint: Start at the left hand column and count across until you reach the car.
steps.done: That is the along value. You read it without anybody teaching you a rule.

steps.pre: Now count up the side. Type the row number your car is parked in.
steps.hint: Start at the bottom row and count upwards until you reach the car.
steps.done: That is the up value. Two numbers, and the car is pinned.

steps.pre: Text it as one number, along first and up second. Type the two digit number.
steps.hint: Put the column number down first, then write the row number straight after it.
steps.done: Order matters. Swap them and your friend walks to the wrong bay.

steps.say: That is a grid reference. Maps do exactly this, but the numbers label the grid lines rather than the bays, and each half has two figures instead of one. Along first, up second: along the corridor, up the stairs. The rest of this lesson is that one habit, first for a whole square, then for a point inside it.

bronze.display: Give the four figure grid reference of the square containing the church.

steps.say: Find the church first. After that it is only reading numbers off the edges.

steps.pre: The church sits in one square. A vertical grid line runs down the left side of that square. Type the two figure number printed under it.
steps.hint: Follow the left hand edge of the church's square straight down to the numbers along the bottom.
steps.done: That is the easting, and it always comes first.

steps.pre: A horizontal grid line runs along the bottom of the same square. Type the two figure number printed beside it.
steps.hint: Follow the bottom edge of the church's square straight across to the numbers up the side.

steps.pre: Join the two pairs, easting first, into one four figure number and type it.
steps.hint: Write the pair you read along the bottom of the map, then the pair you read up the side.

steps.pre: Check it: type the last two figures of the reference you just wrote.
steps.hint: Copy them straight off your own answer, there is nothing new to work out.
steps.done: Those two must be the line you read up the side. If they are not, the halves are the wrong way round and the reference lands in a different square.

steps.say: Bronze move: two lines, the one down the left and the one along the bottom, in that order. Four figures name a whole square, 1 km across.

silver.display:
Give the six figure grid reference of the post office.

This is one grid square from a map, blown up. Its left hand line is 38 and its bottom line is 22. Ticks mark each tenth of the way across and up.

steps.say: The square is already given to you, so the new work is the tenths.

steps.pre: Type the two figure number of the grid line down the left of the square.
steps.hint: It is printed under the left hand edge of the square.
steps.done: That is the first two figures of the easting.

steps.pre: Count the ticks along the bottom. Type how many tenths across the square the post office sits.
steps.hint: Each tick is one tenth, so count from the left hand edge to the dot.
steps.done: That tenth becomes the third figure of the easting.

steps.pre: Type the two figure number of the grid line along the bottom of the square.
steps.hint: It is printed beside the bottom edge of the square.
steps.done: That is the first two figures of the northing.

steps.pre: Count the ticks up the side. Type how many tenths up the square the post office sits.
steps.hint: Each tick is one tenth, so count from the bottom edge up to the dot.

steps.pre: Put the three easting figures first, then the three northing figures, and type the six figure reference.
steps.hint: Line number then tenth for the easting, then line number then tenth for the northing.

steps.pre: Check it: type the last three figures of the reference you just wrote.
steps.hint: Copy them straight off your own answer.
steps.done: Those three must be the northing: the line read up the side, then its tenth. If they are not, the two halves have swapped.

steps.say: Silver move: each half gains a third figure, the tenths. Six figures pin a point to about 100 m.

gold.display:
The road crosses the river at a bridge. Give the six figure grid reference of the bridge.

One grid square, blown up. Its left hand line is 45 and its bottom line is 31. A road (brown) runs across it and a river (blue) winds through it. Nothing is labelled.

steps.say: Nothing is labelled here. The first job is deciding which point on the square you are actually referencing.

steps.pre: The bridge is where the brown road and the blue river meet. Type how many tenths across the square that meeting point sits.
steps.hint: Drop straight down from the crossing point to the ticks along the bottom and count from the left.
steps.done: You have found the feature before touching any numbers. That is the gold habit.

steps.pre: Type the two figure number of the grid line down the left of the square.
steps.hint: It is printed under the left hand edge of the square.

steps.pre: Now the vertical direction. Type how many tenths up the square the crossing point sits.
steps.hint: Track straight across from the crossing point to the ticks on the left and count from the bottom.

steps.pre: Type the two figure number of the grid line along the bottom of the square.
steps.hint: It is printed beside the bottom edge of the square.

steps.pre: Build the reference: easting line, its tenth, northing line, its tenth. Type the six figures.
steps.hint: Three figures for the easting half, then three for the northing half.

steps.pre: Check it: type the first three figures of the reference you just wrote.
steps.hint: Copy them straight off your own answer.
steps.done: Those three must be the easting: the line down the left, then the tenths across. If a river merge or a fork moved, only the tenths would change.

steps.say: Gold move: the question describes the feature instead of naming it. Trace both features, mark where they meet, then reference that exact point.
